subject: FinMetrics — post-demo cost signals and next milestones
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@finmetrics.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finmetrics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: FinMetrics — post-demo cost signals and next milestones

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the candid discussion about where your inference spend is creating friction. Quick recap from my side, plus proposed next steps so we can make progress without back-and-forth.

What you told us (pain signals)
- Monthly GPU spend has spiked ~3x after rollout; billing is noisy (mix of on-demand and bursts).
- 95th pctl latency for user-facing generation occasionally exceeds 400ms and impacts product KPIs.
- Hard to forecast cost per feature due to varying prompt lengths and frequent retries.

Current stack we heard
- In-house inference fleet (NVIDIA A100 + mixed VMs) + a small managed endpoint for experimentation.
- Homegrown cache for common prompts but it’s not integrated with your KV cache across services.

What success looks like (your words)
- Reduce net per-1M inference spend by ~35–45% while keeping p95 generation latency <= 200ms.
- A reproducible test to validate batching/caching without changing core prompts.

Redwood recommendations / signals we discussed
- Continuous micro-batching at the serving runtime for background workloads and strict p99-aware routing for interactive traffic.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated fragments — should shave steady-state token cost by 20–30% on similar workloads.
- Quantization openness: you indicated willingness to evaluate INT8 on non-critical outputs; that’s a realistic path to cost down 30% in certain models.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) We’ll share a simple cost-model template (attached) to capture current token distribution + retry rates — fill by EOD Wed (Apr 7).
2) Technical kickoff (45m) with Karthik + your infra lead to map integration points for caching/batching — proposed slots Thu (Apr 8) or Fri (Apr 9).
3) Run a 2-week controlled test: Redwood provides a config for batching + cache + quantized variant; we’ll run traffic shadowed against your managed endpoint and report delta.

Attachments: cost-model-template.xlsx, inference-config-proposal.pdf

If that aligns, can you confirm who from your infra/eng team should join the kickoff and which date works?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Samantha Li <samantha@finmetrics.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finmetrics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinMetrics — post-demo cost signals and next milestones

Thanks Vanessa — this is super helpful and captures our priorities. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- On quantization: we’re comfortable with INT8 for lower-risk responses (report generation, scheduled summaries). For user-facing chat, we require a blind-A/B to validate impact on quality before broader rollout.
- Cache scope: we can expose a read-only prefix cache for common system prompts but don’t want live writes from Redwood until we validate consistency.
- Procurement: we have an internal budget decision on Apr 21; ideally we’d have a short test and an estimate before then.

For the kickoff, please invite Monica Patel (Customer Success) so she can map success metrics on our side. Our infra lead will be Tom Reynolds (cc’d). Thu Apr 8 at 11:00 PT works for us.

— Sam
Samantha Li
VP Product | FinMetrics
samantha@finmetrics.ai

- 15m: Redwood technical proposal (Karthik) — batching profiles, cache integration options, quantized model variants

Subject: Re: FinMetrics — post-demo cost signals and next milestones

Looping in a couple of technical pointers so we’re aligned for Thu: 

- For batching: please confirm average request size and allowed queueing delay (we typically tune micro-batching to a 20–60ms window for interactive flows).
- For cache: if you can expose the prefix key format we’ll build a read-only hook; we will not write back by default.
- For quantization tests: I plan to run INT8 and FP16 variants in parallel during the 2-week shadow run and measure token-level perplexity drift and human-eval samples.

I’ve attached the minimal infra checklist in the meeting invite. If there’s anything else you want covered, share here and I’ll add to the agenda.

Thanks —
Karthik
Sr Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
